text:
冯唐说：

"穷人的基因，喜欢照顾人，喜欢帮助人；富人遇到不行的人，不做周旋，避免消耗能量；穷人小心翼翼的大方，富人，大大方方的小气。"

冯唐这话，一针见血。

仔细想想身边的人，确实如此。

穷人思维的人，
生怕别人说自己小气，
哪怕自己过得紧巴巴，
也要咬牙请客、硬撑场面。
帮人的时候，自己累得半死，
还不好意思拒绝。
结果呢？
钱花了，力出了，
别人未必领情，
自己倒亏空了一截。

富人思维的人恰恰相反。
不该花的钱，一分不出。
不该帮的忙，一口回绝。
遇到消耗自己的人，
不解释、不纠缠、不周旋，
转身就走，毫不拖泥带水。

不是他们冷血，
是他们算得清一笔账：

你的能量，比你的钱更值钱。

帮一个不值得帮的人，
损失的不仅是时间，还有心情。
维持一段消耗你的关系，
搭进去的不仅是精力，还有运势。

穷人把"被需要"当成了价值，
富人把"不消耗"当成了底线。

穷人花小钱买面子，
富人算大账保里子。

这大概就是，
一个越来越紧，
一个越来越松的根本原因。

所以，该省的时候省，该冷的时候冷。

别把大方用错了地方，
别把好心给错了人。

你的能量很贵，
别随便让人蹭。

你说呢？

完蛋，仇子龙那边出事了。

一项由《Science》与《Retraction Watch》联合调查披露的个案。

2025年3月下旬，上海一所三甲儿科强院收治了一名6岁女童。因CHD3基因单个碱基突变（本应为C、实为T）导致Snijders Blok-Campeau综合征，表现为语言、认知、运动发育落后，但原病不直接危及生命。

家属与仇子龙团队接触后，决定为女儿定制一款面向中枢神经系统的碱基编辑（base editing）疗法，由AAV病毒载体携带编辑器经鞘内注入脑脊液。

家属自筹并获亲友支援合计约86万美元（折合542万人民币）用于该个体化疗法的设计与制备，院方在某项免国家药监局审批的院内/试点通道下放行，伦理委员会签字同意。

text:
So far, Opus 5 feels like a strange but useful in-between of gpt-5.6-sol and Fable 5

It has a lot of Fable's taste, but also comes with gpt-5.6's thoroughness and, well, "autism" (it takes things super literally).

It writes code that is slightly worse to look at than Fable, but more likely to be correct. It regularly is catching things that Fable missed.

So far, feels like a good compromise compared to 5.6's messy code and Fable's habit of being too clever to be correct.

I think I'm gonna like this model a lot.

text:
Anthropic 最近在 Claude Code 博客分享了一套很值得实践的方法：用 Skills 把人工检查变成自动验证循环。

平时的流程通常是 Claude Code 写完代码，你来检查，发现问题后再让它修改。任务虽然交给了 AI，验收环节依然离不开人，最后的瓶颈还是你。

验证循环把这一步也交给系统：

Claude Code 完成修改后自动运行测试，失败就继续定位和修复，直到全部通过才结束。你不需要一直守在旁边，也不用反复提醒它检查同样的问题。

更实用的是自定义 Skill。团队可以把 API 设计规范、PR 描述模板、安全检查清单等内容，写进 .claude/skills/ 下的 Markdown 文件。Claude Code 会在合适的任务中读取并执行，把原本依赖个人记忆的经验变成固定流程。

Claude Code 团队内部已经在串联 /code-review、/simplify、/verify 和设计检查。流程跑稳定后，还能放进每个 PR，成为团队统一的质量门槛。

我觉得最值得动手的第一步很简单：

找出团队里最容易被忘记的一条代码规范，把它写成 Skill，然后实际跑一次。

写进流程里的规范，通常比躺在文档里的规范更有用。

https://t.co/EPipz6B3bU

text:
今天听一个做 AI 的朋友吐槽，说今年是他这辈子过得最“充实”的一年。

这一整年，他把精力全贴进去了：折腾搭网关、跑代理、搞批量注册，每天凌晨三点还在死磕接口为什么又报 502。买服务器、租节点、搭后台，本以为自己终于站在了时代的风口上，结果折腾到最后才发现，是风口在后面撵着他跑。

官方风控只要一升级，账号就得批零重做。昨天还在兴高采烈地规划怎么扩大规模，今天就已经在抓耳挠腮研究今晚接口怎么活下来。

他跟我聊的时候笑得挺无奈，说虽然天天被折磨得够呛，但居然觉得有点过瘾——总觉得自己正在参加一场人类史上的“AI 运维大逃杀”。

奉劝大家千万不要以为，你不喝酒就没事了

我叔上个月就吃了这个亏赔了10万。我叔今年51，开了个五金店。那天他老同学从外地回来，组了局叫了七八个人，他推不掉就去了。

有人带了两瓶白的，我叔说开车不喝酒就喝的茶。饭吃了大概一个多小时，他接到老婆电话说，店里水管爆了让他回去，他打了声招呼就走了。

结果当天夜里出了事，一个同学的喝完回去，就没再醒过来。

家属报警把那天吃饭的人全告了，我叔当时觉得冤得很，他又没喝酒还提前走了，结果法院判了同桌八个人都有责任，我叔赔了10万，其他人各赔了15万。

A woman put a $29 Apple AirTag in her checked luggage at JFK Airport.

The airline lost her bag. The customer service desk said: "We'll locate it and deliver it within 48 hours."

She opened Find My on her iPhone. The bag wasn't at the destination airport. It was at a cargo facility in a different state. Moving. Toward a residential address.

She showed the airline the live GPS location on her phone. They dispatched recovery. The bag  with $3,200 in contents  was returned 6 hours later.

Without the AirTag: she files a claim, waits 3-8 weeks, and receives $1,500-3,800 in airline liability (the maximum under federal regulation). Probably never sees the bag again.

With the AirTag: she tracked it in real time, forced the airline to act, and got everything back.

$29. One coin-sized device. The difference between losing $3,200 and losing nothing.

Apple has sold hundreds of millions of AirTags. Most owners use them for one thing: finding keys. That's a $29 global tracking network being used like a $5 keychain beeper.

Here are 11 AirTag uses and hidden features most owners have never tried 🧵

Introducing celeris-1.

A general purpose language model which delivers near-GPT-5 level intelligence with 15x faster response times.

We’ve developed a new inference architecture that uses diffusion techniques instead of conventional autoregressive generation -  unlocking dramatically better speed while maintaining frontier-level intelligence.

Celeris-1 delivers a p50 response latency of 157ms - around 15× faster than GPT-5-mini and 17× faster than GPT-5 - while scoring comparably 76% on MMLU-Pro, compared with 78% and 81%, respectively.

On tokens per second, Celeris-1 achieves a throughput of 1,280 tokens per second vs 144 for gemini-3.5 flash-light using a reconstructed version of @ArtificialAnlys's  tokens per second benchmark dataset.

🔗：https://t.co/bpnADwlrnf

text:
A senior Anthropic engineer leaked his internal PDF on giving multi-agent systems permanent memory.

Your agent forgets everything the second its context window closes. His fix: a knowledge graph that survives past any single run.

Extract → Resolve → Assemble → Query → Repeat:

Extract: Haiku pulls entities and triples, one call per doc
Resolve: Sonnet matches "Edwin Aldrin" to "Buzz Aldrin" with zero string overlap, just context
Assemble: canonical nodes, typed edges, provenance on every triple
Query: Sonnet reasons over the graph, every answer points to a specific edge

Wire it in as shared memory: workers write to it, evaluators check claims against it, loops run overnight without losing state.

Save this before it gets taken down 👇

text:
Brad Pitt publicly hated Troy (2004) and regretted taking the role. Pitt took the role because he needed to fulfill a commitment after withdrawing from another Warner Bros. project. 

To avoid legal and financial penalties, Brad Pitt agreed to star in Troy instead. 

He called it "a commercial kind of thing," saying the storytelling lacked mystery because the camera was always focused on him as the hero.

Even so, he committed fully to Achilles. Pitt spent nearly 6 months training in sword fighting, boxing, sprinting, and weightlifting, gaining around 10–15 pounds (4.5–7 kg) of lean muscle to resemble ancient Greek statues.

While filming, he ironically tore his Achilles tendon during a battle scene, delaying production.

Looking back, Pitt admitted, "I chunked that scene... I blew that scene. It could be better. I would love another shot at it."

Ironically, many fans and critiques believe that the flatness actually works for Achilles in the film — a character who doesn’t care about anything except winning battles.

text: 老实说，家长这种焦虑就是虚妄和自大。我教了这么多年书，接触过的学生得好几千了，一个CMO金牌水平的都没见过。

quotedTweet.text:
王虹和邓煜同时获得菲尔兹奖，如果把时间倒回到二十年前，很少有人会觉得这两个人最后会站在同一个地方。

邓煜是 IMO 金牌，保送北大，大三进入 MIT，一路都是少年天才的轨迹。王虹则没有任何数学竞赛背景，通过高考进入北大地空学院，第二年才转入数学系。在当时遍地都是奥赛选手的环境里，她一定经历过怀疑，所以才考虑过转去建筑。

一个从一开始就展现出惊人的天赋，一个是在怀疑中慢慢找到自己的方向。谁能想到，二十年后，他们会在数学的最高峰相遇。

有了孩子之后，我难免不焦虑。我身边有很多北大奥赛保送同学，他们的孩子展现出的天赋，确实让我感受到人与人之间的起点并不相同。他们的孩子三岁就会100以内加减法，我的孩子5岁了10以内加减法还得掰手指...

不是每个人都能成为少年天才，但王虹的故事让我相信另一件事：热爱可以抵岁月漫长。

对于大多数人来说，真正的优势未必来自更高的天赋，而是当别人拥有很多选择、不断切换方向的时候，你愿意十年、二十年只做好一件事。长期积累的专注，本身就是一种稀缺的竞争力。

蜗牛和老鹰，都可以到达山顶。

text:
There is a new "Model Router" release almost every day these days and we released ours in April '26. Model routers are becoming an important part of the AI stack as they match each request to the model best suited for it. But routing still produces a singular answer from a singular model. So we are releasing another novel way to improve the $/Intelligent Task. 

@digitalocean's Model Synthesis gets more intelligence from AI, not by choosing a single model but by combining the strengths of several.

Multiple models work on the same problem in parallel. A synthesizer then evaluates their responses, reconciles different perspectives, and produces one stronger answer. Model Synthesis is now available in the DigitalOcean Inference Engine, through a single inference call and the early results are compelling.

On the DRACO deep-research benchmark, an open-model combination of GLM 5.2 and Kimi K2.6 scored higher than every individual model we tested, at just $0.83 per task.

The synthesizer itself proved especially important: choosing the right synthesizer had a greater impact on quality than simply adding more models.Model routing finds the best model for a task.Model synthesis goes further—it assembles the best intelligence for the task.
Learn more here: https://t.co/e5t0FgVAY7
